title: Grateful Dead Live at Oakland Auditorium Arena on 1982-12-28
source: SBD > MC > DAT > CD > EAC > SHN

ai_review.summary: Good soundboard recording of a mixed‑energy show – first set shines with Jack Straw, Lazy Lightning → Deal and Shakedown Street, while the second set feels sleepy
ai_review.review: The SBD source is clear and well‑balanced, though Baby Blue is patched from another tape. The band delivers a solid first set (Jack Straw, Lazy Lightning → Deal, Touch of Grey, Morning Dew) with a standout Shakedown Street that many fans deem an all‑timer despite vocal flubs. Energy wanes in the second half, with a sluggish Terrapin and a generally tired feel.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers praise the first‑set performance and sound quality (average rating ~4.1), but several note a sleepy second set, yielding an overall positive yet mixed assessment.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Clear SBD tape with solid clarity; Baby Blue is patched from another B+‑grade SBD source but otherwise the mix is balanced and listenable.

poor_songs: Terrapin Station (flubbed vocals and weak performance)
show_quality.setlist_flow: First set is praised for tight playing and strong song choices; second set drags with a sleepy vibe, though the Shakedown Street jam recovers some momentum.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Vocal flubs on Shakedown and Terrapin noted; however his solo on Shakedown is called brilliant, funky, and a highlight. Some say he sounds “high” or “a little too fast”.
band_member_comments.Phil: Mentioned as providing a funk‑heartbeat and thumping the groove during Shakedown; praised for deep rhythmic support.
band_member_comments.Bob: Bobby’s Satisfaction rap line is quoted; his humor about lyric flubs and occasional “rap” adds to the show’s character.
band_member_comments.Keys: Brent (keyboards) receives praise for fills, mirroring Jerry, and adding flourishes during Shakedown; overall keyboard work described as psychedelic and supportive.
band_member_comments.Drums: Both drummers are called loose yet funky; noted for deep groove sections in Shakedown and a “wild” feel, though some reviewers felt the drum vibe contributed to the sleepy second set.
